questions.stem: Which part of the Collision Regulations does Rule 38 make up?
options: Part D, Sound and Light Signals
questions.explanation: Rule 38 is the only rule in Part E, Exemptions. Part D, Sound and Light Signals, ends at Rule 37. Parts B and C come earlier.

questions.stem: Which vessels can be exempted under Rule 38?
options: Keel laid before, and meeting the 1960 rules
questions.explanation: Rule 38 covers vessels built, or at a corresponding stage of construction, before the Regulations came into force and complying with the 1960 rules. It is not about length, a general age limit, or ownership.

questions.stem: How long did the Rule 38 exemption from the Annex III sound signal appliance requirements last?
questions.explanation: The exemption for Annex III sound signal appliances lasted nine years from entry into force. Four years applied to some light requirements, and the permanent exemptions are about the position of lights, not sound gear.

questions.stem: Under the Canadian paragraph of Rule 38, the 9-year periods are generally counted from July 15, 1977. Roughly when did those exemptions end?
questions.explanation: Nine years from July 15, 1977 is July 15, 1986. For the vessels whose period starts on March 1, 1983, it ended on March 1, 1992. Either way, these exemptions expired decades ago.

questions.stem: An owner says his 1960s fishing boat is "grandfathered" under Rule 38, so her weak sound signal gear is fine. Which reply is best?
options: Not for sound gear: that 9-year exemption is over
Correct, any vessel built before 1977 is permanently exempt
Correct, as long as she stays in Canadian waters
Correct, as long as she is under 20 metres
questions.explanation: Most Rule 38 exemptions were time-limited. The Annex III sound appliance exemption lasted 9 years and has long expired. The few permanent exemptions relate to the position of lights. Rule 38 is not a blanket exemption based on age, waters or size.
